title: Kernel quickshift scrapbook
content:
09:10 — quick morning dump
- Weird tail-latency spike yesterday on canary (p99 ~ 420ms for short prompt load). Not consistent across regions.
- Hypothesis: small-batch path + KV cache cold leading to synchronous disk reads for quantized embeddings? (unlikely but flagged)
- Repro steps I ran: local perf with small-samples, seed=42, model=rw1-7b-8k, --batch-size=1/2/4, script: tools/bench/run_latency.sh --seq 128.

Immediate TODOs (priority quick wins):
- [ ] Add extra logging around kv_cache.read_stats() in kernel-hotloop (line ~428 in kv_cache.cpp) — want per-request cache hit/miss tags (INF-3421).
- [ ] Smoke test: disable prefix caching on canary for 30m to see impact (rollback plan ready).
- [ ] Compare 1) continuous-batching size distribution vs 2) explicit micro-batches from client. Which path hit the slow code?

Notes from triage with Mina (09:40):
- Mina: saw increased thundering at ~08:15 when a burst of webhook-driven requests replayed. Could be routing causing small bursts hitting same worker.
- Diego: suggested instrumenting request routing tags (route->worker-id) in trace to see hotspots.

Perf experiment plan (quick list):
1) Local repro: run 1000 short prompts, trace p99 with perf counters. Command: PERF_MONITOR=1 ./bin/serve --config test-small-batch.toml > /tmp/run.log
2) Kernel build with extra assert: KERNEL_DEBUG=1 make -C runtime clean && make -j8
3) Try turning off LRU eviction for 10min to see if eviction churn correlates.

Observations/metrics (hand-collected):
- Baseline (yesterday canary): p50 28ms, p95 84ms, p99 420ms (short prompts, seq<=128)
- Local small-run: p50 26ms, p95 90ms, p99 150ms — so local p99 lower than canary; suggests environment or routing effect.

Rough hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Worker hot-queueing due to routing sticky policy -> some workers get microbursts and incur KV eviction thrash. (most likely)
- H2: Rare kernel-path that escalates to fallback allocator on underflow (check allocator logs).
- H3: External network blip to KMS/metrics endpoint causing blocking on critical path (less likely but add check).

Quick patches to try (non-invasive):
- bump continuous-batcher max-delay from 5ms -> 8ms on canary for 1 hour (reduces chances of 1-2 token batches)
- enable route->worker-tagging in traces for two deployments (canary + staging)

Open questions to hash out in async thread:
- If warm workers still experience p99 spikes, is eviction policy maladapted to short-seq workloads? (need data: eviction_count by seq-length)
- Is disk fallback path only for certain quantization flags? Which kernels call vec_read_slow()?

Commands / quick snippets I used today:
- ./tools/bench/run_latency.sh --model rw1-7b --seq 128 --iters 1000 --batching continuous
- git log -n1 --pretty=format:\"%h %s\" runtime/kv_cache.cpp
- perf record -o /tmp/perf.data ./bin/serve --cfg /tmp/test.cfg (then perf report)

Short-term checklist (next 48h):
- [ ] Instrument per-request eviction_count and tag in traces (PR target: today EOD)
- [ ] Run controlled microburst routing test (traffic replay from staging)
- [ ] Confirm there is no KMS/metrics blocking during spike windows (collect tcpdump?)
- [ ] Sync with SRE about circuit-breaker thresholds if router misbehaves

Longer notes / brain dump:
- Might be worth experimenting with tiny adaptive cache: if worker sees > X misses in Y secs, temporarily mark worker"s KV cache as \"aggressive-retain\" (stop evictions for 30s). Danger: memory blow-up — needs guardrails.
- Consider adding a lightweight sampling profiler at the kernel hotloop that emits a 1-line stack sample every 10ms when processing > 100 req/s — cheap but useful for p99 hunts.

Unresolved (to capture thoughts):
- How to reproduce exact canary environment locally? Need env dump from canary run (ask SRE for /etc/container-env dump).
- Is there any correlation with recent rollout (PR 1298) that changed continuous-batcher defaults? Check deploy history.

Slack links / quick references:
- #runtime-triage thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01234XYZ/p1678789200000
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1298
- JIRA: INF-3421 (kv cache tagging)

End notes (12:05):
- Starting with instrumentation PR now. Will ping Mina for canary flip once logs available. If I don't finish before standup, push to tomorrow and leave checklist with Diego.
- Quick morale: keep changes small and observable. Prefer metric-first approaches.

Random TODOs for later (brain snack):
- sketch design for adaptive-cache (one-pager)
- follow up with bench team about 99th percentile harness for short-seq workloads
